one_line_purpose: A high-performance, in-memory key-value cache server built with Python and asyncio, communicating over raw TCP sockets.
problem_solved: Provides a high-performance, in-memory key-value store that can handle concurrent requests, offering fast data retrieval and storage with optional time-to-live (TTL) and Least Recently Used (LRU) eviction policies.
architecture_summary: The KV-Cache server is structured into three main layers: a Network Layer (`tcp_server.py`) utilizing `asyncio` for concurrent TCP connections; a Protocol Layer (`parser.py`, `commands.py`) responsible for parsing custom text-based commands and formatting responses; and a Cache Layer (`store.py`, `eviction.py`) that implements the core key-value storage, Time-To-Live (TTL) management, and a Least Recently Used (LRU) eviction policy. Client requests flow from a TCP socket through the protocol parser to the KV store, and responses are returned accordingly.
key_features: Async TCP server using Python's asyncio for non-blocking I/O
Custom text-based protocol supporting PUT, GET, DELETE, EXISTS, and QUIT commands
Key-value storage with O(1) average-case time complexity for operations
Time-To-Live (TTL) management for automatic key expiration
Least Recently Used (LRU) eviction policy for cache management
Docker image for easy containerization and deployment
Includes benchmarking script for performance analysis of internal components
Includes load testing script for simulating concurrent clients and measuring network performance
notable_code_decisions: Implementation of a custom, simple text-based protocol over raw TCP sockets, providing direct control over communication specifics.
Leveraging Python's `asyncio` for concurrent, non-blocking I/O to efficiently manage multiple client connections.
Utilizing `collections.OrderedDict` for the core KV store and LRU eviction, enabling O(1) average-case time complexity for key operations and LRU order maintenance.
Modular software design with distinct layers for network handling, protocol parsing, and cache logic (store, TTL, eviction) to enhance maintainability and testability.
Provision of command-line arguments and environment variables for flexible server configuration (host, port, max-keys, debug).
Inclusion of comprehensive load testing and benchmarking scripts to validate and measure performance characteristics objectively.
tradeoffs_and_limitations: In-memory storage results in data loss upon server restart or failure, as there is no persistence mechanism.
The custom TCP protocol requires specific client-side implementation (e.g., `scripts/client.py` or `netcat`), lacking compatibility with standard, widely-used client libraries.
The architecture is single-node, which limits scalability beyond the resources of a single machine and presents a single point of failure.
No explicit authentication or authorization mechanisms are provided, making the server insecure for untrusted network environments without external security layers.
The protocol's error handling is basic, relying on simple 'OK'/'ERROR' responses without detailed error codes.
what_it_demonstrates: This project demonstrates the development of a high-performance, asynchronous TCP server using Python's `asyncio`, including the design and implementation of a custom network protocol. It showcases fundamental cache functionalities such as key-value storage, Time-To-Live (TTL), and Least Recently Used (LRU) eviction policies. Furthermore, it exemplifies modular software design, comprehensive testing (unit, integration, load, benchmark), application containerization with Docker, and basic cloud deployment patterns.
